core_themes.name: Consumer experience and interoperability gaps
core_themes.claim: Current chargepoint and hydrogen refuelling networks lack consistent open data, interoperable access, and comparable pricing, leaving consumers facing a fragmented and unreliable experience.

core_themes.name: Electricity system strain and lack of smart functionality
core_themes.claim: Rising EV charging demand will create new pressures on the electricity system, yet most existing and future chargepoints lack the 'smart' communication functionality needed to balance supply and demand.

core_themes.name: Gaps in strategic infrastructure provision
core_themes.claim: Provision of charging and hydrogen refuelling at motorway service areas and fuel retailers is incomplete or underdeveloped, and early-stage hydrogen refuelling infrastructure is commercially unviable without intervention.

core_themes.name: Primary powers for future targeted regulation
core_themes.claim: The Government proposes to take broad primary legislative powers now so that targeted secondary regulation can be introduced if and when needed, rather than fixing detailed requirements immediately.

core_themes.name: Consumer experience measures package
core_themes.claim: The Government proposes powers to mandate open data, interoperable access, transparent pricing and minimum design standards for chargepoints and refuelling stations, favouring flexible, market-based solutions (e.g. bilateral roaming over mandated platforms) over prescriptive mandates.

core_themes.name: Smart charging standards
core_themes.claim: The Government proposes to require minimum 'smart' and open-access functionality in charging infrastructure to enable grid balancing and protect consumers' future access to smart tariffs, based on evidence that such functionality is low-cost to add.

core_themes.name: Strategic provision and hydrogen market support
core_themes.claim: The Government proposes to mandate minimum charging/refuelling provision at motorway service areas and large fuel retailers and to use time-limited franchises to attract private investment in hydrogen refuelling during its commercially unviable growth phase.

core_themes.name: Phased approach via secondary legislation informed by consultation
core_themes.claim: Measures will not take effect without further secondary legislation, with consultation responses and a subsequent Impact Assessment shaping the final scope and timing.

core_themes.name: Principles-led development of smart charging standards
core_themes.claim: Rather than specifying precise technical requirements in primary legislation, Government will set guiding principles (open access, data privacy, security, low energy overhead) and develop detailed standards later through industry engagement.

core_themes.name: Placing obligations on retailers/installers and site operators
core_themes.claim: Government proposes to place compliance obligations on points of sale/installation (retailers and installers) for smart charging, and on MSA operators and large fuel retailers for infrastructure provision, rather than on manufacturers, to ensure practical enforceability and a level playing field.

core_themes.name: Staged civil penalty enforcement regime
core_themes.claim: Compliance will be ensured through an escalating enforcement process—warnings, civil penalties scaled to impact, re-checks and appeal rights—administered by a designated DfT agency.
